questions.hint: Find the new price first, then substitute it into either function.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which situation best illustrates a positive production externality?
options: A firm trains workers who later bring their skills to other firms
A factory pours waste into a river
A consumer buys a healthier meal for themselves
A firm raises the price of its product
questions.answer: A firm trains workers who later bring their skills to other firms
questions.hint: Look for a benefit to third parties arising from the production process.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: With a positive production externality, how are the cost curves positioned?
questions.hint: Society's cost is reduced by the benefit to third parties.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts a carbon tax with a tradable permit scheme?
options: A tax makes the carbon price more certain; permits make the emissions quantity more certain
A tax fixes total emissions exactly; permits fix the price exactly
Both fix emissions and price exactly
Neither gives firms any incentive to cut emissions
questions.answer: A tax makes the carbon price more certain; permits make the emissions quantity more certain
questions.hint: Ask which variable the government sets directly in each case.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In economics, what name is given to government rules or legal standards that directly limit polluting activity?
questions.hint: The firm must obey these limits or face a penalty.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which condition identifies the socially optimal level of output?
options: MSB = MPC only when MPC is zero
questions.hint: It compares the full benefits and full costs to society.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How does an effective awareness campaign about a merit good change the market diagram?
options: MPB shifts to the right, towards MSB
questions.answer: MPB shifts to the right, towards MSB
questions.hint: Better information changes what consumers privately expect to gain.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is a key opportunity cost of subsidising a merit good?
options: Government funds cannot be spent on other priorities
Consumers will pay a much higher price
Producers must stop making the good
questions.answer: Government funds cannot be spent on other priorities
questions.hint: Think about what else the money could have paid for.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the view that a carbon tax is a better response to emissions than a system of tradable permits.
questions.hint: Consider certainty, administration, political acceptability and revenue.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using MSB and MPB, explain why a subsidy on vaccination could increase allocative efficiency. Refer to the welfare loss.
questions.hint: Identify the market failure first, then show how the subsidy changes output.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Discuss whether awareness campaigns are more effective than subsidies for raising the consumption of a merit good.
questions.hint: Consider speed of effect, cost, and consumers with low incomes.

econ-sl.topic: Positive externalities and responses to externalities

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is an example of a positive consumption externality?
options: A vaccinated person lowers the risk of illness for others
A loud party keeps neighbours awake
A factory smokes up a town
questions.answer: A vaccinated person lowers the risk of illness for others
questions.hint: Look for a benefit that reaches other people.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is the external benefit equal to?
questions.hint: It is the gap between society's benefit and the consumer's own benefit.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is the economic term for a good, such as education, that is under-consumed and benefits society as well as the individual?
questions.hint: The term suggests the good deserves to be consumed more.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a market with positive externalities, the free market quantity compared with the social optimum is:
questions.hint: Consumers ignore the benefits to third parties.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The marginal private benefit of a unit is $30 and its external benefit is $8. What is the marginal social benefit, in dollars?
questions.hint: Society's benefit includes both.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A government pays a subsidy of $2 per unit on 5,000 units. How much does this cost the government, in dollars?
questions.hint: Multiply the subsidy by the quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A subsidy paid to producers of a merit good normally shifts which curve, and in which direction?
questions.hint: Think about what happens to producers' costs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why does a carbon tax reduce emissions?
options: It raises the cost of burning fossil fuels, encouraging firms to emit less
It bans all fossil fuels immediately
It removes all costs from polluters
questions.answer: It raises the cost of burning fossil fuels, encouraging firms to emit less
questions.hint: The tax puts a price on something that used to be free.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Under a tradable permit scheme, what can a firm do if it cuts emissions cheaply?
options: Sell its unused permits to other firms
questions.answer: Sell its unused permits to other firms
questions.hint: Permits are valuable to firms that find cuts expensive.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a tradable permit scheme, what do we call the limit set on total emissions?
questions.hint: The scheme is often described with a phrase ending in 'and trade'.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is a drawback of regulation as a response to pollution?
options: It gives firms little reason to cut emissions below the required standard
It requires no monitoring at all
It makes every firm's costs fall
questions.answer: It gives firms little reason to cut emissions below the required standard
questions.hint: What happens after a firm meets the limit?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is an example of a positive production externality?
options: Research by one firm that other firms can also build on
A firm dumping waste into a lake
A shop offering a loyalty discount
questions.answer: Research by one firm that other firms can also build on
questions.hint: The benefit comes from the production side and reaches third parties.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which policy tries to change behaviour mainly by giving people better information?
questions.hint: Think of advertising about the benefits of healthy habits.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain, using MSB and MPB, why education may be under-provided in a free market.
questions.hint: Who gains when one more person is well educated?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the use of subsidies to increase the consumption of a merit good.
questions.hint: Consider both the effect on price and the cost to the government.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Discuss one advantage and one disadvantage of tradable permits compared with direct regulation.
questions.hint: Consider flexibility for firms and the difficulty of setting the cap.

en-hl.topic: The Handmaid's Tale: contexts of production and reception

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In which decade was The Handmaid's Tale first published?
questions.hint: Its context includes the politics of that decade.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the name of the totalitarian regime in the novel?
questions.hint: The name comes from the Bible.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does 'context of production' refer to?
options: The circumstances in which a text was written
The number of copies a text sold
The present-day reader's personal opinion only
questions.answer: The circumstances in which a text was written
questions.hint: Think of the moment of writing, not of reading.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does 'context of reception' refer to?
options: How readers in particular times and places understand a text
The grammar used in a text
The physical size of the book
questions.answer: How readers in particular times and places understand a text
questions.hint: It concerns audiences rather than the author.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which 1980s development is most often linked to the novel's context of production?
options: The growing political influence of the religious right in the United States
The invention of the printing press
The end of the Roman Empire
questions.answer: The growing political influence of the religious right in the United States
questions.hint: Consider the anxieties Gilead appears to exaggerate.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What form do the Historical Notes take?
options: A transcript of an academic conference talk
questions.answer: A transcript of an academic conference talk
questions.hint: Consider who is speaking and to what audience.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In what year is the symposium in the Historical Notes set?
questions.hint: It takes place long after Gilead's end.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the surname of the keynote speaker in the Historical Notes?
questions.hint: He is an academic from the University of Cambridge in the novel.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: According to the Historical Notes, how was Offred's account recorded?
options: In a set of radio broadcasts
questions.hint: Her story was spoken, not written down by her.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What important fact about Gilead do readers learn from the Historical Notes?
options: The regime eventually came to an end
The regime took over the whole world
Gilead never existed in any form
questions.answer: The regime eventually came to an end
questions.hint: The speakers look back on it as history.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main effect of the speaker's jokes in the Historical Notes?
options: They create unease by showing academic detachment from human suffering
They show that the regime was harmless
They prove that Offred invented everything
They make the novel a comedy throughout
questions.answer: They create unease by showing academic detachment from human suffering
questions.hint: Compare his tone with what Offred has endured.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How does the transcribed form of Offred's account affect the reader's trust in the narrative?
options: It reminds readers that the text has been reconstructed and arranged by others
It proves that every detail is exact
It shows that Offred wrote in perfect order
It has no bearing on reliability
questions.answer: It reminds readers that the text has been reconstructed and arranged by others
questions.hint: Who decided the order of the tapes?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Since the late 2010s, why have red cloaks and white bonnets appeared at public protests?
options: To draw attention to concerns about women's rights
To mark the start of a sports event
questions.answer: To draw attention to concerns about women's rights
questions.hint: This shows the novel's image moving into public debate.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Analyse how the Historical Notes change the reader's understanding of Offred's narrative. Refer to tone and narrative perspective.
questions.hint: Consider what the last section adds and what it leaves unresolved.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Discuss how responses to The Handmaid's Tale may have changed between its first publication and the present day.
questions.hint: Think about time and space, adaptation and current debates.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: To what extent does knowledge of the novel's 1980s context of production deepen a modern reader's interpretation? Justify your view with reference to the text.
questions.hint: Weigh what context explains against what the text can say on its own.

en-sl.topic: The Handmaid's Tale: contexts of production and reception

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Gilead is established on the territory of which country in the novel?
questions.hint: The action takes place around Cambridge, Massachusetts.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Who narrates the main part of the novel?
questions.hint: Her name marks her as belonging to a Commander.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: To which genre does the novel most clearly belong?
questions.hint: It imagines a disturbing future society.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which method did the author say she used when inventing Gilead?
options: Including only practices that had some precedent in human history
Inventing every practice with no basis in reality
Basing it only on a fairy tale
questions.answer: Including only practices that had some precedent in human history
questions.hint: This is why the book's warning feels so plausible.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which 1979 revolution is often cited as relevant to the novel's context, because of the new restrictions placed on women?
questions.hint: Notice the date: the event happened only a few years before the novel.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In relation to the debates of the 1970s and 1980s, what does Offred's mother represent?
questions.hint: Remember what Offred recalls her mother taking part in.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the title of the final section of the novel, set far in the future?
accept: Historical Notes on The Handmaid's Tale
questions.hint: It presents the novel as an object of later study.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: On what kind of recording medium was Offred's story found?
questions.hint: It was an everyday technology of the novel's time of writing.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the Historical Notes, what were the recordings found inside?
questions.hint: It is a piece of military-style storage.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How do the academics in the Historical Notes mainly treat Offred's account?
options: As research material to be analysed
As a source of personal guilt
questions.answer: As research material to be analysed
questions.hint: Consider what interests them most about the story.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which question focuses on the novel's context of reception?
options: How have audiences responded since the television adaptation?
What was happening politically when the novel was written?
How many chapters does the novel have?
questions.answer: How have audiences responded since the television adaptation?
questions.hint: Reception concerns audiences after publication.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which question focuses on the novel's context of production?
options: What political anxieties were present when the author wrote?
Why do protesters wear costumes today?
How do schools teach the novel now?
What do online readers post about it?
questions.answer: What political anxieties were present when the author wrote?
questions.hint: Production concerns the time of writing.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why might a reader today respond differently from a reader in 1985?
options: They read it alongside different current events and debates
The words of the novel change each year
They are not allowed to read the ending
The characters have different names now
questions.answer: They read it alongside different current events and debates
questions.hint: Texts stay fixed, but readers' worlds change.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain how the Historical Notes change the way we think about Offred's story.
questions.hint: Consider who controls her words at the end.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain one way the novel's 1980s context of production can be seen in the world of Gilead.
questions.hint: Link a detail of the regime to an anxiety of the time.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why do you think The Handmaid's Tale has received renewed attention in recent years? Support your view with reference to the novel.
questions.hint: Connect a theme in the novel to current public debates.

en_lit-hl.topic: Global issues for the individual oral

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How many fields of inquiry are there for the individual oral?
questions.hint: Try listing them by subject area.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which of these is one of the fields of inquiry?
questions.hint: Fields of inquiry are broad human concerns, not literary features.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which description best fits a global issue for the individual oral?
options: It is significant, transnational and felt in everyday local contexts
It concerns only one character in one work
It is a technical feature of one poem
It is a fact from an author's life
questions.answer: It is significant, transnational and felt in everyday local contexts
questions.hint: Think about scale as well as everyday experience.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which is the best formulated global issue?
options: How unequal access to education limits personal freedom
A metaphor in the opening chapter
The plot of the first act
questions.answer: How unequal access to education limits personal freedom
questions.hint: A good issue is specific and arguable, not one word or a textual detail.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A global issue about climate change most clearly belongs to which field of inquiry?
questions.hint: Consider the natural world and human impact on it.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A global issue about how schools shape moral beliefs most clearly belongs to which field?
questions.hint: Look for the words closest to the issue.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How many minutes of prepared speaking does the individual oral allow?
questions.hint: The teacher's questions come afterwards.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How long is the whole individual oral, in minutes, including the teacher's questions?
questions.hint: Add the teacher's questions to the speaking time.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is the maximum number of lines in the extract chosen from each work?
questions.hint: The extract should be substantial yet focused.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What percentage of the HL Literature assessment is the individual oral worth?
questions.hint: It carries less weight at HL because of the added HL essay.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What combination of works does the Literature individual oral require?
options: One work originally in the language studied and one studied in translation
Two works by the same author
questions.answer: One work originally in the language studied and one studied in translation
questions.hint: The two works should bring different cultural viewpoints.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is the name of the personal collection of reflections and notes kept throughout the course?
questions.hint: It is kept over the two years of the course.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What should a useful portfolio entry for the oral include?
options: Links between passages, authorial choices and an emerging global issue
Only a copy of the plot summary from the internet
A list of the author's awards
questions.answer: Links between passages, authorial choices and an emerging global issue
questions.hint: Think of how it would help you plan your argument.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What should remain central to the oral's analysis?
options: How authorial choices present the global issue in each work
A retelling of each work's plot
The commercial success of each author
questions.answer: How authorial choices present the global issue in each work
questions.hint: Examine the how, not just the what.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Choose two works you have studied. Formulate one global issue they share, name its field of inquiry and justify your choice.
questions.hint: Check that your issue can be seen in both works and in the wider world.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain how narrowing a broad topic such as inequality into a precise global issue can improve an individual oral.
questions.hint: Consider focus, choice of extracts and depth of analysis.

en_lit-sl.topic: Global issues for the individual oral

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How many works must a student use in the individual oral?
questions.hint: One extract comes from each of them.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What percentage of the SL Literature assessment is the individual oral worth?
questions.hint: It has a greater share at SL than at HL.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What term describes a concern with wide impact across borders that is also felt in everyday local life?
questions.hint: This term is the focus of the oral.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits a global issue about belonging in immigrant communities?
questions.hint: Which field concerns who we are and where we belong?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits a global issue about the abuse of authority by governments?
questions.hint: Which field concerns rulers, rights and fairness?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits a global issue about how industrial pollution changes rural life?
questions.hint: Think about the effect on land, water and air.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which field of inquiry best fits a global issue about how storytelling helps people imagine change?
questions.hint: Focus on the power of creating.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which of these is NOT suitable as a global issue?
options: The use of a metaphor in one poem
How poverty limits access to healthcare
How gender expectations restrict career choices
questions.answer: The use of a metaphor in one poem
questions.hint: A global issue extends beyond the text itself.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How long may the extract from each work be?
questions.hint: It must be short enough to discuss in detail.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What follows the student's prepared 10-minute speech?
options: Five minutes of questions from the teacher
A second speech by another student
questions.answer: Five minutes of questions from the teacher
questions.hint: The oral lasts 15 minutes in total.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A work used in the individual oral cannot also be used in which assessment?
questions.hint: Students need a fresh range of works for the comparative essay.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is the main purpose of the learner portfolio?
options: To record personal reflections and develop ideas about the works
To list the prices of books
questions.answer: To record personal reflections and develop ideas about the works
questions.hint: It is a working space for thinking.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which portfolio note is most useful in preparing a global issue?
options: A passage linked to a question about how it shows inequality
A list of the chapter titles only
A note of the book's price
A note of the library's opening hours
questions.answer: A passage linked to a question about how it shows inequality
questions.hint: Useful notes link the text to a wider concern.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain why a good global issue must connect to both of the chosen works.
questions.hint: Think about how the oral compares the works' perspectives.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain how keeping a learner portfolio across the course could help you prepare your individual oral.
questions.hint: Consider what you would forget without a record.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Why do you think the oral asks students to connect literature with real-world issues? Give a reasoned view.
questions.hint: Think about what literature can show that a news report may not.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript of a spoken announcement: « Je vous rappelle que la réunion de jeudi est reportée à lundi prochain, à quatorze heures. » When will the meeting take place?
questions.hint: Listen for the verb reporter and the 24-hour time.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Malgré la pluie, le festival a attiré plus de visiteurs que l'an dernier. » What happened to attendance?
questions.hint: Malgré introduces an obstacle that did not stop the result.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « Je vais magasiner cette fin de semaine avec ma blonde. » These expressions suggest the speaker is most likely from:
questions.hint: Magasiner and fin de semaine are typical of one North American variety.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A Belgian speaker says the price is « nonante-deux euros ». What is the number?
questions.hint: Nonante replaces quatre-vingt-dix.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A Swiss speaker says there are « septante-cinq participants ». How many participants are there?
questions.hint: Septante replaces soixante-dix.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker from France says « quatre-vingt-dix-sept pour cent ». What is the percentage?
questions.hint: Build the number in parts: 4 × 20 + 17.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Le train n'est pas supprimé : il partira simplement avec vingt minutes de retard. » What is true?
options: The train will leave 20 minutes late
questions.answer: The train will leave 20 minutes late
questions.hint: Pay attention to the negative and to the word retard.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Je n'ai jamais dit qu'il fallait interdire les voitures, seulement les limiter en centre-ville. » What is the speaker's position?
options: Cars should be limited in the city centre
There should be more cars in the centre
Cars should not be regulated at all
questions.answer: Cars should be limited in the city centre
questions.hint: Seulement introduces the actual opinion.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: You hear: « Le nombre de jeunes qui lisent la presse a baissé de moitié en dix ans. » Which is the most efficient note?
questions.hint: Good notes keep key data using symbols.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In a listening exam, what is the most useful thing to do before the recording begins?
options: Read the questions and predict likely vocabulary
Write out a full essay plan
Close your eyes and ignore the paper
Translate every word on the page into English
questions.answer: Read the questions and predict likely vocabulary
questions.hint: Prepare your ear for what you might hear.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker uses « en revanche » in the middle of an argument. What does it signal?
questions.hint: Listen for a change of direction after it.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does the French term « prise de notes » mean in English?
questions.hint: Prendre means to take.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « Il pleut des cordes depuis ce matin. » What does this mean?
questions.hint: Idioms should not be taken literally.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « Ah, bravo, encore une grève ! Quelle excellente nouvelle pour les voyageurs ! » What is the speaker's tone?
questions.hint: Compare the positive words with the situation being described.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In 3–5 sentences in French, explain which strategies help you understand a speaker with an unfamiliar francophone accent.
questions.hint: Pensez au contexte, aux mots-clés et à la prédiction.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Certains disent que le télétravail isole les gens, mais moi, j'y vois surtout une liberté : moins de transports, plus de temps en famille. » In 3–5 sentences in French, state the speaker's opinion and justify it with details from the transcript.
questions.hint: Identifiez d'abord l'opinion après le mot mais.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript of a spoken announcement: « Le cours de maths commence à neuf heures et quart. » When does the class begin?
questions.hint: Et quart adds a quarter of an hour.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Aujourd'hui, nous allons parler du recyclage dans notre ville. » What is the topic?
questions.hint: The key word looks like its English equivalent.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « Il y a soixante-dix élèves dans le groupe. » How many students are there?
questions.hint: Think 60 + 10.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « Le voyage dure quatre-vingts minutes. » How many minutes does the trip last?
questions.hint: Think 4 × 20.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In Belgium, what number does « septante » mean?
questions.hint: Sept gives a clue to the first part.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In Québec, what does « la fin de semaine » usually mean?
questions.hint: Fin means end.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Il ne viendra pas ce soir parce qu'il est malade. » What is true?
options: He is not coming because he is ill
He is coming even though he is ill
He is ill but not sure
questions.answer: He is not coming because he is ill
questions.hint: Listen for ne… pas and the reason after parce que.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does the French term « compréhension orale » mean in English?
questions.hint: Orale refers to spoken language.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « Je vais à la bibliothèque après les cours. » In English, name the place the speaker is going to.
questions.hint: A place with many books, though not a bookshop.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does listening for gist mean?
questions.hint: You do not need every detail for this.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: You hear: « Léa va à Paris en train mardi. » Which is the best note?
questions.hint: Keep who, where, how and when.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: A speaker says: « D'abord… ensuite… enfin… » What do these words signal?
questions.hint: They help you follow the order.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « J'aime ce quartier, mais il est trop bruyant. » What is the speaker's view?
options: The speaker likes the area but finds it too noisy
The speaker hates everything about the area
The speaker finds the area too quiet
The speaker has never been there
questions.answer: The speaker likes the area but finds it too noisy
questions.hint: Mais introduces a drawback.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In a listening task, what should you do if you miss a word?
options: Keep listening and use the context
Wait for the speaker to spell it
questions.answer: Keep listening and use the context
questions.hint: The next sentence may help.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In 2–3 sentences in French, say what you do to prepare before a listening exercise.
questions.hint: Pensez aux questions et aux mots-clés.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read this transcript: « Je préfère étudier le matin parce que je suis plus concentré et que la maison est calme. » In 2–3 sentences in French, give the speaker's preference and two reasons.
questions.hint: Cherchez ce qui suit parce que.

geog-hl.topic: Energy security and the energy mix

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What does the term 'energy mix' describe?
options: The combination of energy sources a country uses
The total amount of oil a country exports
The price of electricity for households
The length of a national power grid
questions.answer: The combination of energy sources a country uses
questions.hint: Think about the share each source contributes.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which source generates the largest share of Brazil's electricity?
questions.hint: Consider Brazil's large river basins.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Name the crop used as the main feedstock for Brazil's fuel ethanol.
questions.hint: It is grown widely in São Paulo state.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: The Itaipu Dam, a major source of electricity for Brazil, is built on which river?
questions.hint: It lies on Brazil's south-western border.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which Brazilian region has the greatest concentration of wind power capacity?
questions.hint: Think of the coast and interior exposed to steady trade winds.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which statement best defines energy security?
options: Reliable access to sufficient energy at an affordable price
Producing all energy from renewable sources
Exporting more energy than is imported
Keeping all power stations under state ownership
questions.answer: Reliable access to sufficient energy at an affordable price
questions.hint: A country can import energy and still achieve this.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A country generates 180 TWh from hydropower, 60 TWh from natural gas, 40 TWh from wind and 20 TWh from coal. Calculate the percentage generated from fossil fuels, to 1 decimal place.
questions.hint: Add the two non-renewable sources, then divide by the total.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which is the main energy-security risk of relying heavily on hydropower?
options: Droughts can reduce reservoir levels and output
Water prices are set by international markets
Turbines stop working in cold weather
Dams produce high direct emissions of sulphur dioxide
questions.answer: Droughts can reduce reservoir levels and output
questions.hint: Think about what the source depends on from year to year.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which maritime chokepoint is most important for oil exports from the Persian Gulf?
questions.hint: It connects the Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which Brazilian programme, launched in 1975 after the oil shocks, promoted ethanol as a transport fuel?
questions.hint: Its name refers to alcohol as a fuel.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the key feature of a flex-fuel vehicle?
options: It can run on petrol, ethanol or any blend of the two
It runs only on pure ethanol
It charges its battery from the grid
It uses diesel in winter and petrol in summer
questions.answer: It can run on petrol, ethanol or any blend of the two
questions.hint: Consider the choice a driver has at the pump.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which criticism is most often made of large hydroelectric dams in the Amazon basin?
options: They flood forest and displace local and Indigenous communities
They emit more carbon dioxide per kWh than coal in all cases
They increase the salinity of the Atlantic Ocean
They can only operate during the dry season
questions.answer: They flood forest and displace local and Indigenous communities
questions.hint: Consider the land behind the dam wall.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which of these countries generates the majority of its electricity from nuclear power?
questions.hint: This European country expanded its reactors after the 1970s oil shocks.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Analyse why a diverse national energy mix may improve energy security. Refer to at least two different risks in your answer.
questions.hint: Think about supply disruption, weather and price changes.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Evaluate the claim that sugar cane ethanol is a sustainable energy solution for Brazil.
questions.hint: Weigh emissions and jobs against land use, water and labour conditions.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Discuss how energy resources can be used as a geopolitical tool by exporting countries. Use one example to support your argument.
questions.hint: Consider supply cuts, pricing, pipelines and alliances.

geog-sl.topic: Energy security and the energy mix

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.hint: It will not run out on a human timescale.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
questions.hint: It formed from ancient organic matter underground.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Give the term for generating electricity using the movement of water through turbines.
questions.hint: The first part of the word comes from the Greek for water.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Brazil shares the Itaipu Dam with which neighbouring country?
questions.hint: The country lies directly across the Paraná River.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why is the coast of north-eastern Brazil well suited to wind farms?
options: It has strong, steady trade winds
It has the highest mountains in Brazil
questions.answer: It has strong, steady trade winds
questions.hint: Think about reliability as well as strength.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which action would most directly improve energy security for a country that imports gas from one supplier?
options: Reducing its number of power lines
questions.hint: Consider what happens if that single supplier stops.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A country uses 500 TWh of electricity per year, of which 350 TWh comes from renewable sources. What percentage is renewable?
questions.hint: Divide the renewable part by the total.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the fibrous sugar cane residue that Brazilian mills burn to generate electricity called?
questions.hint: It remains after the juice has been crushed out.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What name is given to Brazil's deep offshore oil reserves, found beneath a thick layer of salt?
questions.hint: The name describes the age of the layer relative to the salt.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the main disadvantage of wind power for a national grid?
options: It produces large amounts of smoke
It cannot be built on land
questions.hint: Consider what happens on a calm day.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which energy source is Iceland's position on a plate boundary especially suited to?
questions.hint: Think about heat rising near volcanic areas.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What was the main cause of Brazil's electricity rationing in 2001?
options: Low reservoir levels after a period of low rainfall
A war with a neighbouring country
The closure of all wind farms
questions.answer: Low reservoir levels after a period of low rainfall
questions.hint: Recall which source dominated Brazil's electricity at that time.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the main purpose of OPEC?
options: To coordinate oil production policies among member states
To build wind farms in developing countries
To regulate electricity prices in Europe
To manage all shipping through the Suez Canal
questions.answer: To coordinate oil production policies among member states
questions.hint: The final letter stands for exporting countries.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which fuel does the pipeline from Bolivia to Brazil carry?
questions.hint: It is a gaseous fossil fuel, burned in power stations and industry.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain two advantages for Brazil of generating much of its electricity from hydropower.
questions.hint: Think about the country's physical geography and emissions.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain how conflict in a major energy-exporting region can affect the energy security of an importing country.
questions.hint: Consider both physical supply and world prices.

hist-hl.topic: Paper 1 skills: source content and the inquiry question

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In IB History Paper 1, what does 'source content' refer to?
options: What the source states or shows
Who paid for the source to be published
Which historian wrote about the source
questions.answer: What the source states or shows
questions.hint: Separate this from judging its value.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What is the function of the inquiry question at the top of a source task?
options: It defines what you should look for in the source
It lists the facts you must memorise
It tells you the source's author
It gives you the mark scheme
questions.answer: It defines what you should look for in the source
questions.hint: It sets the focus of your reading.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which is the most precise use of a source?
options: The writer's claim that 'bread prices doubled within a month' indicates rapid inflation.
The source is about the economy and problems.
The writer says many things about food.
questions.answer: The writer's claim that 'bread prices doubled within a month' indicates rapid inflation.
questions.hint: Look for a brief quotation linked to a point.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented letter from 1932: 'Since the factory closed in March, half the men on our street have no wage. We queue for soup twice a week, and my sister has sold her sewing machine.' What does it reveal about unemployment?
options: Families lost income and sold possessions to survive
The government had solved the crisis
Wages were rising in the writer's street
questions.answer: Families lost income and sold possessions to survive
questions.hint: Use the details about wages, soup and the sale.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented letter from 1932: 'We queue for soup twice a week, and my sister has sold her sewing machine.' What item was sold?
questions.hint: Look for the object in the second half of the sentence.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented report: 'The new ration cards were issued on Monday. By Thursday the northern bakeries had no flour, yet the officials' canteen served white bread.' What does it imply?
options: Officials had the same food as everyone else
questions.hint: Compare the situation in the two places named.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: An inquiry question asks what a source reveals about women's employment during a war. Which response stays on source content?
options: The source states that women 'now run the tram lines', showing they took on transport jobs.
The source is limited because it was written by a journalist.
The war began after a long diplomatic crisis.
Many historians disagree about the war's causes.
questions.answer: The source states that women 'now run the tram lines', showing they took on transport jobs.
questions.hint: Choose the answer drawn from what the source says about the question's topic.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: When a task asks what a source 'suggests', what should your answer contain?
options: An inference supported by evidence from the source
A list of dates from your notes
An evaluation of the source's origin
questions.answer: An inference supported by evidence from the source
questions.hint: You are moving beyond the literal, but not beyond the evidence.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What term describes a conclusion drawn from evidence when a source does not state it directly?
questions.hint: It comes from a verb meaning to work something out.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: An invented poster shows a giant worker lifting a factory above a broken city, with the words 'Together we rebuild'. What message does it most clearly convey?
options: Collective labour will restore the nation
questions.answer: Collective labour will restore the nation
questions.hint: Consider both the image and the slogan.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which feature would most weaken a source-content answer?
options: Long copied quotations with no link to the question
Short quotations explained in the student's own words
Separate points for separate pieces of evidence
Direct reference to the inquiry question
questions.answer: Long copied quotations with no link to the question
questions.hint: Examiners want to see understanding, not transcription.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented speech: 'We shall ask no sacrifice our farmers cannot bear; yet the grain quotas must be met by the end of harvest.' What tension does it reveal?
options: Reassurance alongside firm demands on farmers
Complete freedom for farmers to set quotas
An end to the collection of grain
A plan to replace all farmers with soldiers
questions.answer: Reassurance alongside firm demands on farmers
questions.hint: Compare the clause before 'yet' with the clause after it.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A source-content question is worth 3 marks. As a good working rule, how many distinct relevant points should you aim to make?
questions.hint: Link the number of points to the marks available.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented diary entry from 1941: 'The sirens went at nine again. We carried the children to the cellar, and no one spoke of the school, closed now for a month.' What does it reveal about the effects of air raids on civilian life? Refer to the source.
questions.hint: Look at both routine and disruption, and use short references.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain why short, embedded quotations usually make a source-content answer stronger than general description.
questions.hint: Think about precision and how an examiner checks understanding.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain the difference between stating what a source reveals and evaluating its value and limitations for a historian.
questions.hint: One concerns content; the other concerns origin and purpose.

hist-sl.topic: Paper 1 skills: source content and the inquiry question

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How many sources are normally provided in an IB History Paper 1 document set?
questions.hint: It is enough for comparison and synthesis.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which skill is mainly tested when you are asked what a source reveals?
options: Memorising the date of the source
questions.hint: Focus on what is in the source.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Before reading a source closely, what should you identify first?
options: The focus of the inquiry question
The number of words in the source
The longest word in the source
Your favourite part of the topic
questions.answer: The focus of the inquiry question
questions.hint: Decide what you are looking for.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which sentence uses evidence most effectively?
options: The reference to 'empty market stalls' suggests severe food shortages.
The source is interesting and useful.
Food is discussed in the source.
questions.answer: The reference to 'empty market stalls' suggests severe food shortages.
questions.hint: Look for a quotation joined to a point.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented newspaper extract from 1919: 'Dockers walked out on Tuesday, demanding shorter hours; by Friday, the tram crews had joined them.' What does it reveal about the strike?
options: It spread to other groups of workers
It was opposed by all tram crews
It was about lower rents only
questions.answer: It spread to other groups of workers
questions.hint: Compare who was involved on Tuesday and on Friday.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented newspaper extract from 1919: 'Dockers walked out on Tuesday, demanding shorter hours.' What did the dockers demand?
questions.hint: Find the words after 'demanding'.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented teacher's note from 1946: 'Thirty-eight pupils share eleven books, and the roof still leaks over the back row.' What does it suggest about schools after the war?
options: Schools had more books than pupils
questions.hint: Use both the books and the roof.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: An invented cartoon shows a tiny clerk holding back a huge wave labelled 'Prices'. What is its most likely message?
options: Clerks enjoy working at the seaside
Floods caused the banking system to close
questions.hint: Think about the difference in size between the figure and the wave.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A question asks what a source reveals about rural poverty. Which answer is off-focus?
options: The source was written by a government official, so it may be biased.
The source's mention of 'barefoot children' suggests families lacked basic goods.
The phrase 'one meal a day' indicates hunger.
The reference to 'unpaid rents' shows families were in debt.
questions.answer: The source was written by a government official, so it may be biased.
questions.hint: Which answer moves from content to evaluation?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What makes a reference to a source 'precise'?
options: It points to specific words or details
It mentions the source's overall topic
It names a general historical period
questions.answer: It points to specific words or details
questions.hint: Could the examiner find it in the source immediately?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Complete the term used for what a source shows or states: source ____.
questions.hint: It is the opposite focus to origin and purpose.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented minute of a town meeting: 'The council voted to open the hall as a shelter, though three members objected to the cost.' What does it reveal?
options: The council supported the shelter despite some disagreement
All council members rejected the shelter
The shelter was free from any cost debate
questions.answer: The council supported the shelter despite some disagreement
questions.hint: Use both the decision and the objection.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: A source-content question is worth 2 marks. As a good working rule, how many distinct relevant points should you aim to make?
questions.hint: Link the number of points to the marks available.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Read this invented letter from 1933: 'The mill now runs three days a week. Father mends boots at night, and we have let the upstairs room to a lodger.' What does it reveal about how families responded to economic hardship? Refer to the source.
questions.hint: Identify more than one way the family adapted.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain why you should avoid adding lots of your own knowledge when answering a question about what a source reveals.
questions.hint: Think about what the task is asking you to do.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain how you would use the inquiry question to decide which details from a source to include.
questions.hint: Consider relevance and how to select evidence.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: State the x-coordinate of the vertex of y = 2(x - 3)² + 5.
questions.hint: Compare with the form a(x - h)² + k.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Write x² - 6x + 11 in the form (x - h)² + k.
questions.hint: Complete the square using half the coefficient of x.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the discriminant of 2x² - 5x + 3.
questions.hint: Use b² - 4ac.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: How many real roots does x² + 4x + 7 = 0 have?
questions.hint: Check the sign of the discriminant.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve x² - 5x - 14 < 0.
questions.hint: Factorise, then consider where the parabola is below the x-axis.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the set of values of k for which x² + kx + 9 = 0 has no real roots.
questions.hint: Set the discriminant to be negative.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the remainder when x³ - 2x² + 4x - 5 is divided by x - 2.
questions.hint: Use the remainder theorem: evaluate at the root of the divisor.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Given that x - 2 is a factor of x³ + ax² - 4x + 12, find a.
questions.hint: Set p(2) = 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: When 2x³ + x² - 3x + k is divided by x + 1, the remainder is 7. Find k.
questions.hint: Evaluate the polynomial at x = -1.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the sum of the roots of 3x³ - 6x² + 5x - 9 = 0.
questions.hint: Use -(coefficient of x²) divided by the leading coefficient.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the product of the roots of 2x⁴ - 3x³ + x - 8 = 0.
questions.hint: Use (-1)ⁿ × constant term ÷ leading coefficient.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The roots of 2x² - 7x + 4 = 0 are α and β. Find the exact value of α² + β².
questions.hint: Use α² + β² = (α + β)² - 2αβ.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Factorise x³ - 7x + 6 fully.
questions.hint: Try small integer values to find a first factor.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: If a quadratic has a discriminant of zero, what does its graph do?
options: Touches the x-axis at exactly one point
Crosses the x-axis at two points
questions.answer: Touches the x-axis at exactly one point
questions.hint: Think about equal roots.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The height of a ball is h(t) = -5t² + 20t + 3 metres. Find its maximum height.
questions.hint: Find the t-value of the vertex first.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain why a cubic polynomial with real coefficients must have at least one real root.
questions.hint: Consider the behaviour of the graph as x tends to positive and negative infinity.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve x² - 7x + 10 = 0.
questions.hint: Find two numbers with product 10 and sum 7.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve 3ˣ = 81.
questions.hint: Write 81 as a power of 3.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve log₂ x = 5.
questions.hint: Rewrite in exponential form.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve ln x = 0.
questions.hint: What power of e gives this value?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which substitution is most useful for solving x⁴ - 5x² + 4 = 0?
questions.hint: Notice that x⁴ is the square of another power of x.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the sum of the two positive solutions of x⁴ - 5x² + 4 = 0.
questions.hint: Let u = x², solve for u and take positive square roots.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the sum of the solutions of 2²ˣ - 6 × 2ˣ + 8 = 0.
questions.hint: Let u = 2ˣ, then solve the quadratic in u.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve 5ˣ = 12, giving your answer exactly as a logarithm.
questions.hint: Take a logarithm with a convenient base.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use a graphical method or GDC to find the positive solution of eˣ = x + 2. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Find where the two curves intersect for x > 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solving f(x) = g(x) is equivalent to finding which of these?
questions.hint: Move all terms to one side.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which equation is best solved using a graphical method on a GDC?
questions.hint: Which equation combines different types of function?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve log₁₀ x + log₁₀(x - 3) = 1.
questions.hint: Combine the logs, then check any solution in the original equation.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: When solving log₁₀ x + log₁₀(x - 3) = 1, why is x = -2 rejected?
options: The logarithm of a negative number is not defined
It is smaller than the base
questions.answer: The logarithm of a negative number is not defined
questions.hint: Substitute the value into the first log.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The line y = 2x + 3 meets the curve y = x² at two points. Find the y-coordinate of the point with positive x.
questions.hint: Solve x² = 2x + 3 first.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: How many real solutions does x³ = x have?
questions.hint: Rearrange and factorise fully.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain when an analytic method is more appropriate than a graphical method for solving an equation, and give one reason a GDC might still be useful.
questions.hint: Think about exact answers and checking.

phys-hl.topic: B.5 Current and circuits: charge, potential difference and resistance

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which is the definition of electric current?
questions.hint: Think of charge passing a point per second.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A charge of 12 C passes a point in 4.0 s. Calculate the current in A.
questions.hint: Use I = Q / t.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A current of 2.0 A flows for 30 s. Calculate the charge transferred in C.
questions.hint: Rearrange I = Q / t.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: 24 J of energy is transferred when 3.0 C of charge moves between two points. Calculate the potential difference in V.
questions.hint: Potential difference is energy per unit charge.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A resistor has a current of 0.50 A with a potential difference of 6.0 V across it. Calculate its resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Use the definition R = V / I.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What does the I–V graph of an ohmic conductor look like at constant temperature?
options: A straight line through the origin
A curve that flattens at high voltage
questions.answer: A straight line through the origin
questions.hint: Current is directly proportional to potential difference.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: How does the resistance of a filament lamp change as the current increases?
questions.hint: Consider the temperature of the filament.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A uniform wire's length is doubled while its cross-sectional area is unchanged. What happens to its resistance?
questions.hint: Use R = ρL / A.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A copper wire has resistivity 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m, length 10 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m². Calculate its resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Use R = ρL / A.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: The diameter of a uniform wire is doubled, with no change in length or material. By what factor does its resistance change? Give a decimal.
questions.hint: Area depends on the square of the diameter.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: State the SI unit of resistivity.
questions.hint: Rearrange R = ρL / A to find the unit.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A metal wire has charge carrier density 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³ and cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m². It carries a current of 2.0 A, and each carrier has charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Calculate the drift speed in mm s⁻¹, to 2 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use I = nAvq, then convert from m s⁻¹.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Why does the resistance of a metal wire usually increase with temperature?
options: Lattice ions vibrate more, so electrons collide more often
More free electrons are released per atom
The wire's charge carriers become positive
The electrons stop drifting at higher temperatures
questions.answer: Lattice ions vibrate more, so electrons collide more often
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the atoms in the lattice.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω is connected to a 5.0 Ω resistor. Calculate the terminal potential difference in V.
questions.hint: Find the current first, then subtract the voltage lost inside the cell.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A student finds the gradient of the tangent to a non-ohmic I–V curve and says this gives the resistance at that point. Explain why this is incorrect and describe how to find the resistance correctly.
questions.hint: Use the definition of resistance at a single point.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain, in terms of charge carriers and energy, how a resistor transfers energy from a circuit to its surroundings.
questions.hint: Consider collisions of electrons with the lattice.

phys-sl.topic: B.5 Current and circuits: charge, potential difference and resistance

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.hint: One ampere for one second transfers one of these units.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which is the definition of potential difference?
questions.hint: Consider what a volt is equal to.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A current of 0.80 A flows for 10 s. Calculate the charge transferred in C.
questions.hint: Use Q = It.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A current of 5.0 A flows for 60 s. Calculate the charge transferred in C.
questions.hint: Multiply current by time in seconds.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A 9.0 V potential difference is applied across a 3.0 Ω resistor. Calculate the current in A.
questions.hint: Use V = IR.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A current of 0.25 A passes through a 40 Ω resistor. Calculate the potential difference across it in V.
questions.hint: Use V = IR.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: 18 J of energy is transferred when 2.0 C of charge moves through a component that carries a current of 3.0 A. Calculate the resistance of the component in Ω.
questions.hint: Find the potential difference first.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Under which condition does a metal conductor obey Ohm's law?
options: When it is carrying alternating current only
questions.hint: Think about what can alter resistance during a test.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What feature does the I–V graph of an ideal diode show?
options: It conducts significantly in only one direction
It conducts equally in both directions
It has constant resistance for all voltages
questions.answer: It conducts significantly in only one direction
questions.hint: Compare the positive and negative parts of the graph.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: On an I–V graph (I on the y-axis) for an ohmic conductor, what does the gradient represent?
questions.hint: Rearrange V = IR into the form y = mx.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A wire has resistivity 5.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m, length 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m². Calculate its resistance in Ω.
questions.hint: Use R = ρL / A.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A wire's cross-sectional area is increased, with length and material unchanged. What happens to its resistance?
questions.hint: Think about how much room there is for charge to flow.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: How many electrons, each of charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, carry a total charge of 1.6 C?
questions.hint: Divide total charge by the charge of one electron.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A component carries 0.20 A with a potential difference of 3.0 V across it. Calculate its resistance at this point in Ω.
questions.hint: Use R = V / I, using the values at that point.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain why a filament lamp is a non-ohmic component.
questions.hint: Link the current to temperature and then to resistance.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Describe how you would determine the resistivity of a metal wire in the laboratory.
questions.hint: Think about what to measure and which graph to plot.

psych-hl.topic: Thinking and decision-making: heuristics and cognitive biases

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is a heuristic?
options: A mental shortcut used to make judgements
A brain region involved in memory
A research method used in experiments
questions.answer: A mental shortcut used to make judgements
questions.hint: Think about making decisions quickly.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which description fits System 1 in dual-process models?
questions.hint: Think of responses that occur without deliberate effort.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which description fits System 2 in dual-process models?
questions.hint: Think about solving a hard problem step by step.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which bias occurs when an initial number influences a later estimate?
questions.hint: The term comes from something that holds a boat in place.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: After seeing much news coverage of plane crashes, someone overestimates their frequency. Which heuristic best explains this?
questions.hint: Which examples come to mind most easily?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is the name of the effect in which the wording of equivalent information changes decisions?
questions.hint: The term relates to how something is presented, as with a picture.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: In classic framing research, what do people tend to prefer when options are described in terms of lives saved?
questions.hint: Think about attitudes to risk when gains are in focus.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which error is shown by judging 'a bank clerk who is also an activist' as more likely than 'a bank clerk'?
questions.hint: Can two events together be more probable than one of them alone?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is confirmation bias?
options: Favouring information that supports existing beliefs
Remembering the last item on a list
Believing an outcome was inevitable after it happens
questions.answer: Favouring information that supports existing beliefs
questions.hint: Consider what evidence a person chooses to notice.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: In prospect theory, what does loss aversion mean?
options: Losses feel larger than equivalent gains
Gains feel larger than equivalent losses
questions.answer: Losses feel larger than equivalent gains
questions.hint: Compare losing a sum with winning that same sum.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: In a classic anchoring study, participants saw a rigged wheel stop on a high or low number before estimating a quantity. What was the main result?
options: Estimates were unaffected by the wheel
All participants gave the correct answer
questions.hint: The number was irrelevant, but did it still matter?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which is a common limitation of laboratory research on decision-making?
questions.hint: Consider how artificial the tasks can be.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Research in which legal experts were still influenced by irrelevant numbers when suggesting sentences best supports which conclusion?
options: Expertise does not fully remove anchoring
Only students are subject to anchoring
Anchoring never occurs in real settings
questions.answer: Expertise does not fully remove anchoring
questions.hint: Consider what this means for experienced decision-makers.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Explain how a dual-process model can account for errors in everyday decision-making.
questions.hint: Consider what happens when intuitive responses are not checked.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Evaluate the use of laboratory experiments to investigate heuristics and cognitive biases.
questions.hint: Weigh control and causation against realism and generalisability.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Discuss the extent to which heuristics should be regarded as errors rather than useful strategies.
questions.hint: Think about speed and accuracy in different environments.

psych-sl.topic: Thinking and decision-making: heuristics and cognitive biases

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which task is an example of System 1 thinking?
questions.hint: Which response happens quickly and without effort?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which task most clearly requires System 2 thinking?
options: Reading a large road sign in your first language
questions.hint: Which task demands focused mental effort?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is a cognitive bias?
questions.hint: The key idea is that the error follows a pattern.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which heuristic involves judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind?
questions.hint: Think about information that is readily accessible.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A shop displays a high 'original price' next to a sale price. Which bias is it using?
questions.hint: The first number becomes a reference point.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Describing a treatment as having '90% survival' rather than '10% mortality' is an example of what?
questions.hint: The facts are the same; the presentation differs.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A bat and a ball cost £1.10 in total. The bat costs £1.00 more than the ball. How many pence does the ball cost?
questions.hint: Write an equation rather than trusting your first impression.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Tomás is quiet and loves books, so someone assumes he is a librarian rather than a salesperson, ignoring how many people do each job. Which heuristic is being used?
questions.hint: He seems to match a stereotype.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is the bias of seeking information that supports what you already believe?
questions.hint: It concerns evidence that agrees with a prior view.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Why are heuristics useful in everyday life?
options: They save time and mental effort
They replace the need for memory
questions.answer: They save time and mental effort
questions.hint: Think about having limited time and information.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Under which conditions are people most likely to rely on System 1?
options: Under time pressure or when tired
When given unlimited time and clear instructions
When a decision has been written out in full
questions.answer: Under time pressure or when tired
questions.hint: Consider when effortful thinking is harder.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A framing study does not tell participants its exact aim in advance. Which ethical step is most important afterwards?
options: Paying them only if they answer correctly
questions.hint: Think about what participants should learn after taking part.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: In an experiment testing the framing effect, what is the independent variable?
questions.hint: What does the researcher deliberately change?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which is a common limitation of using only university students in decision-making research?
options: Findings may not generalise to other populations
Heuristics do not occur in students
questions.answer: Findings may not generalise to other populations
questions.hint: Think about who the sample represents.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Explain one heuristic, using an original example from everyday life.
questions.hint: Say what the shortcut is and how it influenced the decision.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Explain one strength and one limitation of using experiments to study decision-making.
questions.hint: Think about control and realism.
